title: Location-based field tasks
question: Can an AI agent create a field inspection checklist for a place that someone can open on their phone?
answer: Yes, without code. A chatbot writes https://gismap.online/?workflow=tasks#fieldTask=json:<URI-encoded JSON> with the title, location, coordinates, notes and up to ten steps. The person in the field checks in, ticks off steps and sends back a report link. No account or server is involved.
triggers: Make a field inspection checklist for this park
Create five tasks to do on site at this address
Send someone to check these locations
inputTypes: Features of a public layer (by object ID)

required.name: tasks
required.description: The things to do; five per package by default.

optional.name: instructions
optional.description: Notes for the person (up to 500 characters).

optional.name: features
optional.description: Up to five features to visit, by layer URL and object ID.

steps.action: Read llms.txt, this recipe and api/capabilities.json; note the engine and execution environment you actually have.
Resolve the location to coordinates (or pick features by object ID from a real layer).

Write the task: id, title, location, latitude, longitude, notes, steps [{ text }], optional features [{ layerUrl, objectId, latitude, longitude, label }]. Requests for more than five tasks become several packages ('… 1 of 2') with the same id prefix; never drop one.

Without code: write https://gismap.online/?workflow=tasks#fieldTask=json:<encodeURIComponent(JSON)> with { title, location, lat, lon, notes, steps: ["…"], features: [{ layerUrl, objectId, lat, lon, label }] }. With code: createFieldTaskUrl from "https://gismap.online/js/field-task-share.js" for a compact, QR-safe link.
Decode the link (decodeFieldTask) and compare title, location and every step; with a browser, open it and confirm the task panel, map location and check-in button.
Return the assignment link (QR-safe). The completed report comes back as a separate link made by the person in the field.

artifact.structure: One task package: title, location, coordinates, notes, steps (checklist), features to visit; returned reports add check-in, steps done, notes, who and when.

outputs.notes: Links are kept under 2,800 characters; the app's Share dialog draws one.
Created by the field worker in the app, never by the agent.

verification: All requested tasks present, five per package
Steps, title and notes decode unchanged
Mobile task panel opens with check-in and steps
limitations: Each task is a checklist step: steps have text only, not separate IDs, evidence types or completion rules.
Photos stay on the field device and go into the PDF report; links never carry them. A check-in records place and time, not proof that the work was done.
Up to 10 steps, 5 features and 500 characters of notes per package; progress persists only in the report link the worker sends back.
recovery: If the link is too long, shorten notes and step text or split the package.
Never fabricate a check-in, photo or completed report.

examples.title: Mission Dolores Park inspection
examples.prompt: Create five inspection tasks for a city park: playground structures, damaged equipment photos, drinking fountains, pedestrian paths, litter and maintenance.
checks: Opened headless: the task panel showed the title, location, five steps and check-in; screenshot inspected.
No check-in or report was made: those belong to a real field visit.

examples.title: Mission Dolores Park inspection, readable link
examples.prompt: Same task, as a link a chatbot can write without code.
checks: #fieldTask=json: form; opened headless from this branch (local server): task panel with five steps and check-in (screenshot inspected).
